facts.value: autocephaly recognized at the Council of Ephesus, 431. Tradition names Barnabas as founder

citations.excerpt: The Patriarchate of Antioch wanted to place the church under its jurisdiction, but the Council of Ephesus in 431, and later the emperor, recognized the autocephaly of the Church of Cyprus.
The Apostle Barnabas is regarded as the founder and first bishop of the local church

facts.value: The Orthodox church of Cyprus. Under French and Venetian rule from 1191 to 1570 the conquerors introduced a Latin hierarchy.

citations.excerpt: The period of French (1191-1489) and Venetian rule (1489-1570/1) that followed lasted for almost four centuries. The conquerors introduced a Latin hierarchy and took control of church affairs.

facts.value_before_verify: The autocephalous Orthodox church of Cyprus, under a Latin hierarchy during French and Venetian rule from 1191 to 1570.
